    Random node

    The Random node is a transient routing screen that chooses one connected output by relative weight on the next service Tick. It does not Show or Hide a View itself.

    Configure outputs

    Add entries under Random Outputs, give each one a non-negative finite Weight, and connect it to one UI or Action chain. The percentages shown beside ports are calculated from connected outputs only.

    For example, connected weights 1, 1, and 2 produce approximate shares of 25%, 25%, and 50%. The absolute scale does not matter: 10, 10, and 20 produce the same result.

    The graph validator requires:

    • at least one connected output;
    • one target per connected output;
    • every Weight to be finite and zero or greater;
    • the sum of connected Weights to be greater than zero.

    Disconnected outputs show 0% and are ignored by runtime selection.

    Note

    In version 0.2.0, Random still shows inherited Node Description and Clear History fields in the Inspector, but the compiler does not copy them to the Random runtime node. In particular, Clear History has no runtime effect on Random.

    Runtime behavior

    After navigation enters Random, UINavigationService.Tick() selects a branch on the next update. If its Action chain reaches another screen, navigation uses a normal Push transition; a terminal Action branch only executes its Actions. Put Action nodes between Random and the target when the chosen branch should also change time scale, log, or manage a scene.

    Use Random for loot screens, rotating tips, A/B flows, or any route whose probability belongs in the graph rather than application code.
